newsitem.title: USA: Rexrodt says inflation on G7 agenda, not a threat.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says inflation on G7 agenda, not a threat.

text.p: German economics minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Saturday that inflation as a topic was back on the agenda at this weekend meeting of the Group of Seven industrialized nations, but that no immediate threat was seen.

Rexrodt told a breakfast briefing here, "The subject of inflation has come up again. There is no urgent problem ...and I cannot imagine that we will find a ready solution. But the issue is in the air again."
In clear reference to the fact that strong growth in the U.S. economy is raising fears of inflation, Rexrodt added, "The U.S. economy is generally excellent."
Rexrodt was in Denver for a summit meeting of government leaders of the Group of Seven industrialized nations. The G7 groups Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
